morningSummary:
Wednesday, 18 November 2026 — Night News. Updated at 21:00 Europe/Paris. Presented by Sophie Laurent.

MIDDLE EAST — ADNOC Logistics & Services says one crew member is missing and 11 were injured after one of its vessels was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz. Oman separately reported rescuing 24 crew members from the LPG tanker Tara Gas, with one person still missing and a fire-fighting operation continuing. Saudi-led coalition strikes hit Houthi-held areas in Yemen; casualty figures are attributed to Houthi authorities. Israeli forces launched a new ground operation in central Gaza, prompting displaced residents to flee; Israel and Hamas give sharply different accounts of the operation.

NIGERIA — President Bola Tinubu has received the state-police constitutional amendment bill after all 36 state assemblies approved it. He says he will consult the Attorney-General before a formal signing ceremony. The separate National Policing Bill is still being developed. The ADC says it has filed a 17-ground appeal and asks the Court of Appeal to preserve party and candidate records; its interim request is not yet a court order. The Senate has also called for investigations into electoral violence and fair access to public campaign venues.

ASIA-PACIFIC — Donald Trump arrived in Shenzhen and was welcomed by Xi Jinping. Xi and Vladimir Putin held talks; Trump and Putin are expected to meet Thursday. Trump claimed a major trade deal with the Philippines, but Manila says details remain to be worked out and no agreement has been signed.

EUROPE — US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are expected in Berlin on Thursday for discussions with Ukrainian and European officials on security guarantees and reconstruction. France's 17 November public-sector protests drew 146,000 participants according to the Interior Ministry and more than 500,000 according to the CGT.

AFRICA — The UN has verified at least 2,230 civilian deaths in Sudan from January to October, including more than 1,630 linked to drone strikes; the actual toll may be higher. South Africa's foreign minister says the diplomatic reprimand involving Nigeria's High Commissioner is a closed matter.

INTERNATIONAL JUSTICE — The International Court of Justice is scheduled to deliver its judgment in The Gambia v Myanmar at 10:00 a.m. on Thursday, 19 November. The judgment has not yet been delivered.

BUSINESS AND TECHNOLOGY — Nvidia's record results have not removed investor concerns about AI valuations. Markets continue to weigh energy supply risks, technology investment and trade policy.

featured.title: Hormuz attack leaves one crew member missing and 11 injured as shipping risks mount
featured.summary: ADNOC Logistics & Services says one crew member is missing and 11 were injured after one of its vessels was attacked while transiting the Strait of Hormuz. Oman separately reported rescuing 24 crew members from the Panama-flagged LPG tanker Tara Gas, with one person still missing and a fire-fighting operation under way.
featured.content: ADNOC Logistics & Services confirmed that one of its vessels was attacked on Tuesday evening, 17 November. The company said one crew member remained unaccounted for, 11 were injured and the remaining crew had been evacuated. Reuters reported that maritime security sources described a projectile strike on an LPG tanker. Separately, Oman's emergency authorities said they rescued 24 crew members from the Panama-flagged Tara Gas and were continuing a search for one missing person while dealing with a fire aboard. Because ADNOC did not identify its vessel in its statement, the two sets of details should not be merged without confirmation. The incidents add to a surge in attacks and disruption affecting commercial shipping through the strait.

topStories.title: APEC: Trump arrives in Shenzhen; Xi and Putin hold talks ahead of Thursday meetings
topStories.summary: Donald Trump has arrived in Shenzhen and was welcomed by Xi Jinping. Xi and Vladimir Putin have held talks, while a Trump-Putin meeting is expected Thursday and wider trilateral discussions involving Xi remain in focus.
topStories.content: At the APEC summit in Shenzhen, Chinese President Xi Jinping welcomed US President Donald Trump. Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin have also held talks, and Trump and Putin were seen greeting each other as leaders gathered for the summit. US officials say Trump and Putin are expected to meet on Thursday. A broader trilateral discussion involving Xi has been widely anticipated, but no three-leader agreement has been announced. The agenda is expected to include trade, the war in Ukraine, Iran and wider security questions. The leaders' public statements and any formal joint communique will matter more than speculation about a breakthrough.

topStories.title: ADC asks Court of Appeal to preserve party and candidate records as 17-ground challenge proceeds
topStories.summary: The African Democratic Congress says it has filed a 17-ground appeal against the 5 November Federal High Court judgment affecting its leadership. It has asked the Court of Appeal to restrain INEC from changing party and candidate records while the appeal is pending.
topStories.content: The ADC says its appeal challenges the Federal High Court's jurisdiction, the claimant's standing, the assessment of disputed evidence and the orders made in the leadership dispute. The party is asking the Court of Appeal to preserve its existing leadership records and nomination particulars, including those connected with its presidential and governorship candidates, while the appeal is considered. The filing is a legal step, not proof that the appellate court has granted the requested interim relief. INEC's obligations and the party's leadership status remain subject to applicable court orders and further judicial decisions.

topStories.title: Tinubu receives state-police constitutional amendment bill after approval by all 36 state assemblies
topStories.summary: President Bola Tinubu has received the constitutional amendment bill seeking to establish state police after all 36 State Houses of Assembly approved it. The President says he will review it with the Attorney-General before a formal signing ceremony.
topStories.content: The proposed Sixth Alteration to the 1999 Constitution has secured approval from all 36 state legislatures, exceeding the constitutional threshold reported by the National Assembly. The Senate directed that the bill be transmitted to the President, and the Presidency confirmed on Wednesday that Tinubu had received it. Chief of Staff Femi Gbajabiamila said the President would consult the Attorney-General before assenting at a formal ceremony. The constitutional amendment is not yet in force simply because it has been received. A separate National Policing Bill is still being developed to provide the operational framework. The reform raises important questions about accountability, funding, training, judicial oversight and safeguards against political abuse at state level.

topStories.source: Channels Television; Premium Times; Punch Newspapers
topStories.whyItMatters: State police could change Nigeria's security architecture, but safeguards and clear operational rules will be essential.
topStories.whatHappensNext: Watch for the President's decision, the formal assent process and the separate National Policing Bill.
topStories.label: NIGERIA GOVERNANCE

topStories.title: Israeli forces launch new ground operation in central Gaza as displaced families flee
topStories.summary: Israeli forces have begun a new ground operation in central Gaza. Israel says troops are targeting Hamas infrastructure, while Hamas calls the operation a ceasefire violation. Dozens of displaced Palestinians reportedly fled the area.
topStories.content: Reuters reports that Israeli tanks advanced along the Salahudeen road across the Yellow Line in central Gaza. The Israeli military said the operation was aimed at Hamas infrastructure. Hamas described the move as a dangerous escalation and a breach of the October 2025 ceasefire. Dozens of displaced residents were reported to have fled after evacuation instructions and gunfire. Palestinian medics reported casualties in several incidents, while the Israeli military disputed or said it was unaware of some accounts. The parties continue to accuse each other of violating the ceasefire. The situation remains fluid, and casualty claims should be attributed to the relevant sources.

topStories.title: US envoys expected in Berlin for Ukraine talks on security guarantees and reconstruction
topStories.summary: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are expected in Berlin on Thursday to meet Ukrainian officials and a European negotiating team, a US official says.
topStories.content: The planned discussions are expected to focus on credible post-war security guarantees for Ukraine, a comprehensive economic recovery plan and preparation for another round of multilateral negotiations. The meetings follow recent contacts involving Russian, Ukrainian and US officials in Abu Dhabi and talks between the US envoys and Vladimir Putin in Moscow. Despite public suggestions of progress, Russia and Ukraine remain far apart on territory and security arrangements. The Berlin meeting has not yet taken place, and no agreement should be presumed.

topStories.title: Ukraine says second strike damaged Crimean Bridge and collapsed a road span
topStories.summary: Ukraine's military and security services say a second strike damaged the Crimean Bridge and caused a road span to collapse. Russia has acknowledged damage and opened a terrorism investigation; independent confirmation of all Ukrainian claims remains limited.
topStories.content: Ukrainian officials say an operation on the Kerch, or Crimean, Bridge caused a section of the road span to fall into the water after a second night of strikes. Kyiv says the operation involved several weapons and services. Russian authorities confirmed damage, opened a terrorism case and said the bridge would be repaired. The bridge is a strategic road and rail link between Russia and occupied Crimea. Reporting on the precise extent of damage and the weapons used relies heavily on statements from the parties to the war, so those details should remain attributed rather than treated as independently established.

topStories.title: France protests: unions report more than 500,000 participants; Interior Ministry counts 146,000
topStories.summary: Demonstrations over wages and purchasing power continued on 17 November. The Interior Ministry counted 146,000 participants nationwide, while the CGT union claimed more than 500,000.
topStories.content: Public-sector unions called demonstrations demanding higher wages, joined by private-sector workers and young people. France's Interior Ministry estimated turnout at 146,000 nationwide, while the CGT union claimed more than 500,000. The marches were largely peaceful, but participation and the movement's momentum remain contested. Protesters say wages and public services have failed to keep pace with living costs. Union leaders are also seeking to influence the debate ahead of the April 2027 presidential election. The competing crowd figures should be attributed to their respective sources rather than presented as a single agreed count.

topStories.title: UN verifies more than 2,230 civilian deaths in Sudan conflict through October
topStories.summary: The UN Human Rights Office says it verified at least 2,230 civilian deaths in Sudan between January and October 2026, including more than 1,630 linked to drone strikes. It warns the actual toll is likely higher.
topStories.content: A report by the UN Human Rights Office documents the devastating civilian impact of Sudan's war between the Sudanese Armed Forces, the Rapid Support Forces and allied armed groups. The UN says at least 2,230 civilians were killed from January to the end of October, with more than 1,630 deaths caused by drone strikes. Markets, hospitals, schools, fuel facilities, water sources and civilian vehicles have been hit. The Kordofan region accounted for more than two-thirds of verified civilian deaths. The UN says some violations may amount to war crimes and calls for accountability and protection of civilians. These are verified minimum figures, not a complete count of all deaths.

topStories.title: Saudi-led coalition strikes Houthi targets in Yemen as attacks spread across the region
topStories.summary: A Saudi-led coalition has launched major strikes on Houthi-held areas, saying it targeted missile warehouses and drone workshops. Houthi authorities report at least 17 deaths; the casualty claims have not been independently verified.
topStories.content: The Associated Press reports that the Saudi-led coalition struck locations in Sanaa and three provinces. Houthi authorities said at least 17 people were killed, including 15 at a sponge factory in Hodeida. The coalition described its targets as missile warehouses and drone workshops. The Houthis also said they fired missiles towards Riyadh, while Saudi air defences reported intercepting them. Claims about targets and casualties remain attributed to the parties and reporting agencies. The strikes add another front to an already volatile regional security situation.

topStories.title: Trump claims major US-Philippines trade deal, but Manila says details still need to be worked out
topStories.summary: Donald Trump announced what he called a major trade deal with the Philippines, but Reuters reports that Manila described a more cautious understanding on economic cooperation and said trade representatives would need to turn commitments into concrete initiatives.
topStories.content: Speaking during a visit to Manila, Trump said the two countries had concluded a very large and mutually fair trade deal, but did not provide detailed terms. The Philippine President's office described the outcome more cautiously as an understanding on economic cooperation. The Philippine ambassador said the United States had offered help diversifying food and energy supplies and confirmed that nothing had been signed. The announcement should therefore not be presented as a completed, fully published treaty. Further details and formal documentation are needed to establish the scope of any commitments.

topStories.whyItMatters: The Philippines is seeking stronger trade and energy resilience while balancing its security and economic ties with Washington and Beijing.
topStories.whatHappensNext: Look for published terms, signatures and confirmation from both governments.
topStories.label: TRADE WATCH

topStories.title: ICJ set to deliver landmark judgment in The Gambia's Rohingya genocide case on Thursday
topStories.summary: The International Court of Justice is scheduled to deliver its judgment at 10:00 a.m. local time on Thursday, 19 November, in The Gambia's case alleging violations of the Genocide Convention by Myanmar.
topStories.content: The International Court of Justice has confirmed that its public sitting will take place at the Peace Palace in The Hague at 10:00 a.m. on Thursday. The case concerns allegations that Myanmar violated the Genocide Convention through its treatment of the Rohingya people. Myanmar has disputed the allegations and described its 2017 military campaign as a counterterrorism operation. The court's judgment will be legally significant, although enforcement ultimately depends on state compliance and international mechanisms. The ruling has not yet been delivered as of Wednesday night.

topStories.whyItMatters: The judgment could shape international accountability for genocide and influence future interpretation of states' obligations under the Convention.
topStories.whatHappensNext: Follow the court's official judgment and distinguish its legal findings from commentary about wider conflicts.

topStories.title: South Africa formally reprimands Nigeria's envoy after public broadcasting dispute
topStories.summary: South Africa's foreign ministry summoned Nigeria's High Commissioner Femi Fani-Kayode after a public dispute over coverage of his credentials ceremony. Pretoria says diplomatic concerns should be raised through official channels.
topStories.content: South Africa's Department of International Relations and Cooperation has formally reprimanded Nigeria's High Commissioner, Femi Fani-Kayode, after he complained that his introduction and speech were excluded from an SABC broadcast of his credentials ceremony. The Nigerian envoy disputed the handling of the event, while South African officials said diplomatic concerns should be channelled through the relevant institutions and foreign ministries. The disagreement comes amid wider sensitivities in bilateral relations, including concerns about attacks on foreign nationals. The public exchange is a diplomatic disagreement; it should not be confused with a formal rupture in relations.

topStories.source: allAfrica; South African Department of International Relations and Cooperation
topStories.whyItMatters: Relations between two major African economies matter for trade, migration, regional diplomacy and the safety of citizens abroad.
topStories.whatHappensNext: Look for responses from Nigeria's foreign ministry and any diplomatic steps to resolve the dispute.
topStories.label: AFRICA DIPLOMACY

topStories.title: Nvidia posts record revenue but AI-market anxiety weighs on shares
topStories.summary: Nvidia reported another quarter of record revenue and raised its guidance, but its shares fell as investors questioned the durability of the AI trade. Markets also watched oil and Federal Reserve signals.
topStories.content: The Wall Street Journal's market coverage reports that Nvidia announced record quarterly revenue and lifted its outlook, yet its shares declined and failed to lift broader technology stocks. Investors remain concerned about valuations and the scale of spending required to sustain artificial-intelligence growth. Other AI-linked companies also weakened, while traders awaited Federal Reserve minutes and further signals on interest rates. Oil prices eased as higher US inventories offset some of the risk premium from renewed Gulf fighting. A single trading session does not establish a long-term reversal in the AI sector, but it shows how sensitive markets have become to expectations.

topStories.whyItMatters: AI investment affects technology valuations, data-centre spending, employment and global semiconductor supply chains.
topStories.whatHappensNext: Watch company guidance, capital expenditure plans, Fed communications and the next trading sessions.
topStories.label: MARKETS

worldNews.summary: A Saudi-led coalition has launched major strikes on Houthi-held areas, saying it targeted missile warehouses and drone workshops. Houthi authorities report at least 17 deaths; the casualty claims have not been independently verified.
worldNews.content: The Associated Press reports that the Saudi-led coalition struck locations in Sanaa and three provinces. Houthi authorities said at least 17 people were killed, including 15 at a sponge factory in Hodeida. The coalition described its targets as missile warehouses and drone workshops. The Houthis also said they fired missiles towards Riyadh, while Saudi air defences reported intercepting them. Claims about targets and casualties remain attributed to the parties and reporting agencies. The strikes add another front to an already volatile regional security situation.

usaNews.title: Trump claims major US-Philippines trade deal, but Manila says details still need to be worked out
usaNews.summary: Donald Trump announced what he called a major trade deal with the Philippines, but Reuters reports that Manila described a more cautious understanding on economic cooperation and said trade representatives would need to turn commitments into concrete initiatives.
usaNews.content: Speaking during a visit to Manila, Trump said the two countries had concluded a very large and mutually fair trade deal, but did not provide detailed terms. The Philippine President's office described the outcome more cautiously as an understanding on economic cooperation. The Philippine ambassador said the United States had offered help diversifying food and energy supplies and confirmed that nothing had been signed. The announcement should therefore not be presented as a completed, fully published treaty. Further details and formal documentation are needed to establish the scope of any commitments.

usaNews.title: Nvidia posts record revenue but AI-market anxiety weighs on shares
usaNews.summary: Nvidia reported another quarter of record revenue and raised its guidance, but its shares fell as investors questioned the durability of the AI trade. Markets also watched oil and Federal Reserve signals.
usaNews.content: The Wall Street Journal's market coverage reports that Nvidia announced record quarterly revenue and lifted its outlook, yet its shares declined and failed to lift broader technology stocks. Investors remain concerned about valuations and the scale of spending required to sustain artificial-intelligence growth. Other AI-linked companies also weakened, while traders awaited Federal Reserve minutes and further signals on interest rates. Oil prices eased as higher US inventories offset some of the risk premium from renewed Gulf fighting. A single trading session does not establish a long-term reversal in the AI sector, but it shows how sensitive markets have become to expectations.

electionWatch.title: ADC files 17-ground appeal and asks Court of Appeal to protect candidate records
electionWatch.summary: The African Democratic Congress says it has filed a 17-ground appeal against the judgment affecting its leadership and Atiku Abubakar's candidacy. It has asked the Court of Appeal to restrain INEC from altering party and candidate records while the appeal is pending.
electionWatch.content: The ADC has disclosed a 17-ground appeal challenging the Federal High Court judgment delivered on 5 November in the leadership dispute involving the party. The party argues, among other points, that the trial court lacked jurisdiction and that the claimant's standing and disputed evidence were not properly assessed. It has also asked the Court of Appeal to preserve existing leadership records and candidate nomination particulars pending determination of the appeal. This is an application by the party, not confirmation that the appellate court has granted the requested restraint. The legal position remains subject to the courts' decisions and INEC's lawful obligations.

articles.title: Hormuz attack leaves one crew member missing and 11 injured as shipping risks mount
articles.summary: ADNOC Logistics & Services says one crew member is missing and 11 were injured after one of its vessels was attacked while transiting the Strait of Hormuz. Oman separately reported rescuing 24 crew members from the Panama-flagged LPG tanker Tara Gas, with one person still missing and a fire-fighting operation under way.
articles.content: ADNOC Logistics & Services confirmed that one of its vessels was attacked on Tuesday evening, 17 November. The company said one crew member remained unaccounted for, 11 were injured and the remaining crew had been evacuated. Reuters reported that maritime security sources described a projectile strike on an LPG tanker. Separately, Oman's emergency authorities said they rescued 24 crew members from the Panama-flagged Tara Gas and were continuing a search for one missing person while dealing with a fire aboard. Because ADNOC did not identify its vessel in its statement, the two sets of details should not be merged without confirmation. The incidents add to a surge in attacks and disruption affecting commercial shipping through the strait.

articles.summary: Donald Trump has arrived in Shenzhen and was welcomed by Xi Jinping. Xi and Vladimir Putin have held talks, while a Trump-Putin meeting is expected Thursday and wider trilateral discussions involving Xi remain in focus.
articles.content: At the APEC summit in Shenzhen, Chinese President Xi Jinping welcomed US President Donald Trump. Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin have also held talks, and Trump and Putin were seen greeting each other as leaders gathered for the summit. US officials say Trump and Putin are expected to meet on Thursday. A broader trilateral discussion involving Xi has been widely anticipated, but no three-leader agreement has been announced. The agenda is expected to include trade, the war in Ukraine, Iran and wider security questions. The leaders' public statements and any formal joint communique will matter more than speculation about a breakthrough.

articles.title: ADC asks Court of Appeal to preserve party and candidate records as 17-ground challenge proceeds
articles.summary: The African Democratic Congress says it has filed a 17-ground appeal against the 5 November Federal High Court judgment affecting its leadership. It has asked the Court of Appeal to restrain INEC from changing party and candidate records while the appeal is pending.
articles.content: The ADC says its appeal challenges the Federal High Court's jurisdiction, the claimant's standing, the assessment of disputed evidence and the orders made in the leadership dispute. The party is asking the Court of Appeal to preserve its existing leadership records and nomination particulars, including those connected with its presidential and governorship candidates, while the appeal is considered. The filing is a legal step, not proof that the appellate court has granted the requested interim relief. INEC's obligations and the party's leadership status remain subject to applicable court orders and further judicial decisions.

articles.title: Tinubu receives state-police constitutional amendment bill after approval by all 36 state assemblies
articles.summary: President Bola Tinubu has received the constitutional amendment bill seeking to establish state police after all 36 State Houses of Assembly approved it. The President says he will review it with the Attorney-General before a formal signing ceremony.
articles.content: The proposed Sixth Alteration to the 1999 Constitution has secured approval from all 36 state legislatures, exceeding the constitutional threshold reported by the National Assembly. The Senate directed that the bill be transmitted to the President, and the Presidency confirmed on Wednesday that Tinubu had received it. Chief of Staff Femi Gbajabiamila said the President would consult the Attorney-General before assenting at a formal ceremony. The constitutional amendment is not yet in force simply because it has been received. A separate National Policing Bill is still being developed to provide the operational framework. The reform raises important questions about accountability, funding, training, judicial oversight and safeguards against political abuse at state level.

articles.source: Channels Television; Premium Times; Punch Newspapers
articles.whyItMatters: State police could change Nigeria's security architecture, but safeguards and clear operational rules will be essential.
articles.whatHappensNext: Watch for the President's decision, the formal assent process and the separate National Policing Bill.

articles.title: Israeli forces launch new ground operation in central Gaza as displaced families flee
articles.summary: Israeli forces have begun a new ground operation in central Gaza. Israel says troops are targeting Hamas infrastructure, while Hamas calls the operation a ceasefire violation. Dozens of displaced Palestinians reportedly fled the area.
articles.content: Reuters reports that Israeli tanks advanced along the Salahudeen road across the Yellow Line in central Gaza. The Israeli military said the operation was aimed at Hamas infrastructure. Hamas described the move as a dangerous escalation and a breach of the October 2025 ceasefire. Dozens of displaced residents were reported to have fled after evacuation instructions and gunfire. Palestinian medics reported casualties in several incidents, while the Israeli military disputed or said it was unaware of some accounts. The parties continue to accuse each other of violating the ceasefire. The situation remains fluid, and casualty claims should be attributed to the relevant sources.

articles.title: Ukraine says second strike damaged Crimean Bridge and collapsed a road span
articles.summary: Ukraine's military and security services say a second strike damaged the Crimean Bridge and caused a road span to collapse. Russia has acknowledged damage and opened a terrorism investigation; independent confirmation of all Ukrainian claims remains limited.
articles.content: Ukrainian officials say an operation on the Kerch, or Crimean, Bridge caused a section of the road span to fall into the water after a second night of strikes. articles.content: Public-sector unions called demonstrations demanding higher wages, joined by private-sector workers and young people. articles.title: UN verifies more than 2,230 civilian deaths in Sudan conflict through October
articles.summary: The UN Human Rights Office says it verified at least 2,230 civilian deaths in Sudan between January and October 2026, including more than 1,630 linked to drone strikes. It warns the actual toll is likely higher.
articles.content: A report by the UN Human Rights Office documents the devastating civilian impact of Sudan's war between the Sudanese Armed Forces, the Rapid Support Forces and allied armed groups. The UN says at least 2,230 civilians were killed from January to the end of October, with more than 1,630 deaths caused by drone strikes. Markets, hospitals, schools, fuel facilities, water sources and civilian vehicles have been hit. The Kordofan region accounted for more than two-thirds of verified civilian deaths. The UN says some violations may amount to war crimes and calls for accountability and protection of civilians. These are verified minimum figures, not a complete count of all deaths.

articles.title: Saudi-led coalition strikes Houthi targets in Yemen as attacks spread across the region
articles.summary: A Saudi-led coalition has launched major strikes on Houthi-held areas, saying it targeted missile warehouses and drone workshops. Houthi authorities report at least 17 deaths; the casualty claims have not been independently verified.
articles.content: The Associated Press reports that the Saudi-led coalition struck locations in Sanaa and three provinces. Houthi authorities said at least 17 people were killed, including 15 at a sponge factory in Hodeida. The coalition described its targets as missile warehouses and drone workshops. The Houthis also said they fired missiles towards Riyadh, while Saudi air defences reported intercepting them. Claims about targets and casualties remain attributed to the parties and reporting agencies. The strikes add another front to an already volatile regional security situation.

articles.summary: Donald Trump announced what he called a major trade deal with the Philippines, but Reuters reports that Manila described a more cautious understanding on economic cooperation and said trade representatives would need to turn commitments into concrete initiatives.
articles.content: Speaking during a visit to Manila, Trump said the two countries had concluded a very large and mutually fair trade deal, but did not provide detailed terms. The Philippine President's office described the outcome more cautiously as an understanding on economic cooperation. The Philippine ambassador said the United States had offered help diversifying food and energy supplies and confirmed that nothing had been signed. The announcement should therefore not be presented as a completed, fully published treaty. Further details and formal documentation are needed to establish the scope of any commitments.

articles.title: ICJ set to deliver landmark judgment in The Gambia's Rohingya genocide case on Thursday
articles.summary: The International Court of Justice is scheduled to deliver its judgment at 10:00 a.m. local time on Thursday, 19 November, in The Gambia's case alleging violations of the Genocide Convention by Myanmar.
articles.content: The International Court of Justice has confirmed that its public sitting will take place at the Peace Palace in The Hague at 10:00 a.m. on Thursday. The case concerns allegations that Myanmar violated the Genocide Convention through its treatment of the Rohingya people. Myanmar has disputed the allegations and described its 2017 military campaign as a counterterrorism operation. The court's judgment will be legally significant, although enforcement ultimately depends on state compliance and international mechanisms. The ruling has not yet been delivered as of Wednesday night.

articles.title: South Africa formally reprimands Nigeria's envoy after public broadcasting dispute
articles.summary: South Africa's foreign ministry summoned Nigeria's High Commissioner Femi Fani-Kayode after a public dispute over coverage of his credentials ceremony. Pretoria says diplomatic concerns should be raised through official channels.
articles.content: South Africa's Department of International Relations and Cooperation has formally reprimanded Nigeria's High Commissioner, Femi Fani-Kayode, after he complained that his introduction and speech were excluded from an SABC broadcast of his credentials ceremony. The Nigerian envoy disputed the handling of the event, while South African officials said diplomatic concerns should be channelled through the relevant institutions and foreign ministries. The disagreement comes amid wider sensitivities in bilateral relations, including concerns about attacks on foreign nationals. The public exchange is a diplomatic disagreement; it should not be confused with a formal rupture in relations.

articles.title: Nvidia posts record revenue but AI-market anxiety weighs on shares
articles.summary: Nvidia reported another quarter of record revenue and raised its guidance, but its shares fell as investors questioned the durability of the AI trade. Markets also watched oil and Federal Reserve signals.
articles.content: The Wall Street Journal's market coverage reports that Nvidia announced record quarterly revenue and lifted its outlook, yet its shares declined and failed to lift broader technology stocks. Investors remain concerned about valuations and the scale of spending required to sustain artificial-intelligence growth. Other AI-linked companies also weakened, while traders awaited Federal Reserve minutes and further signals on interest rates. Oil prices eased as higher US inventories offset some of the risk premium from renewed Gulf fighting. A single trading session does not establish a long-term reversal in the AI sector, but it shows how sensitive markets have become to expectations.

africaNews.content: The Associated Press reports that the Saudi-led coalition struck locations in Sanaa and three provinces. Houthi authorities said at least 17 people were killed, including 15 at a sponge factory in Hodeida. The coalition described its targets as missile warehouses and drone workshops. The Houthis also said they fired missiles towards Riyadh, while Saudi air defences reported intercepting them. Claims about targets and casualties remain attributed to the parties and reporting agencies. The strikes add another front to an already volatile regional security situation.

nigeriaNews.title: ADC asks Court of Appeal to preserve party and candidate records as 17-ground challenge proceeds
nigeriaNews.summary: The African Democratic Congress says it has filed a 17-ground appeal against the 5 November Federal High Court judgment affecting its leadership. It has asked the Court of Appeal to restrain INEC from changing party and candidate records while the appeal is pending.
nigeriaNews.content: The ADC says its appeal challenges the Federal High Court's jurisdiction, the claimant's standing, the assessment of disputed evidence and the orders made in the leadership dispute. The party is asking the Court of Appeal to preserve its existing leadership records and nomination particulars, including those connected with its presidential and governorship candidates, while the appeal is considered. The filing is a legal step, not proof that the appellate court has granted the requested interim relief. INEC's obligations and the party's leadership status remain subject to applicable court orders and further judicial decisions.

nigeriaNews.title: Tinubu receives state-police constitutional amendment bill after approval by all 36 state assemblies
nigeriaNews.summary: President Bola Tinubu has received the constitutional amendment bill seeking to establish state police after all 36 State Houses of Assembly approved it. The President says he will review it with the Attorney-General before a formal signing ceremony.
nigeriaNews.content: The proposed Sixth Alteration to the 1999 Constitution has secured approval from all 36 state legislatures, exceeding the constitutional threshold reported by the National Assembly. The Senate directed that the bill be transmitted to the President, and the Presidency confirmed on Wednesday that Tinubu had received it. Chief of Staff Femi Gbajabiamila said the President would consult the Attorney-General before assenting at a formal ceremony. The constitutional amendment is not yet in force simply because it has been received. A separate National Policing Bill is still being developed to provide the operational framework. The reform raises important questions about accountability, funding, training, judicial oversight and safeguards against political abuse at state level.

nigeriaNews.title: Senate calls for investigations into electoral violence and equal access to public campaign venues
nigeriaNews.summary: The Senate has urged investigations into political violence and called on governors to ensure opposition parties have fair access to public campaign venues.
nigeriaNews.content: The resolution comes amid growing activity ahead of the 2027 general election. Lawmakers have called for investigations into attacks linked to political campaigns and for public facilities to be made available fairly to political parties. In Kaduna, the ADC says it was denied access to a stadium for a rally, while the state government disputes the party's account of the correspondence. These competing accounts should be assessed through documents and independent verification. The broader issue is whether all parties can campaign safely and on equal terms.

asiaNews.title: APEC: Trump arrives in Shenzhen; Xi and Putin hold talks ahead of Thursday meetings
asiaNews.summary: Donald Trump has arrived in Shenzhen and was welcomed by Xi Jinping. Xi and Vladimir Putin have held talks, while a Trump-Putin meeting is expected Thursday and wider trilateral discussions involving Xi remain in focus.
asiaNews.content: At the APEC summit in Shenzhen, Chinese President Xi Jinping welcomed US President Donald Trump. Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin have also held talks, and Trump and Putin were seen greeting each other as leaders gathered for the summit. US officials say Trump and Putin are expected to meet on Thursday. A broader trilateral discussion involving Xi has been widely anticipated, but no three-leader agreement has been announced. The agenda is expected to include trade, the war in Ukraine, Iran and wider security questions. The leaders' public statements and any formal joint communique will matter more than speculation about a breakthrough.

asiaNews.title: Trump claims major US-Philippines trade deal, but Manila says details still need to be worked out
asiaNews.summary: Donald Trump announced what he called a major trade deal with the Philippines, but Reuters reports that Manila described a more cautious understanding on economic cooperation and said trade representatives would need to turn commitments into concrete initiatives.
asiaNews.content: Speaking during a visit to Manila, Trump said the two countries had concluded a very large and mutually fair trade deal, but did not provide detailed terms. The Philippine President's office described the outcome more cautiously as an understanding on economic cooperation. The Philippine ambassador said the United States had offered help diversifying food and energy supplies and confirmed that nothing had been signed. The announcement should therefore not be presented as a completed, fully published treaty. Further details and formal documentation are needed to establish the scope of any commitments.

asiaNews.title: ICJ set to deliver landmark judgment in The Gambia's Rohingya genocide case on Thursday
asiaNews.summary: The International Court of Justice is scheduled to deliver its judgment at 10:00 a.m. local time on Thursday, 19 November, in The Gambia's case alleging violations of the Genocide Convention by Myanmar.
asiaNews.content: The International Court of Justice has confirmed that its public sitting will take place at the Peace Palace in The Hague at 10:00 a.m. on Thursday. The case concerns allegations that Myanmar violated the Genocide Convention through its treatment of the Rohingya people. Myanmar has disputed the allegations and described its 2017 military campaign as a counterterrorism operation. The court's judgment will be legally significant, although enforcement ultimately depends on state compliance and international mechanisms. The ruling has not yet been delivered as of Wednesday night.

businessNews.title: Nvidia posts record revenue but AI-market anxiety weighs on shares
businessNews.summary: Nvidia reported another quarter of record revenue and raised its guidance, but its shares fell as investors questioned the durability of the AI trade. Markets also watched oil and Federal Reserve signals.
businessNews.content: The Wall Street Journal's market coverage reports that Nvidia announced record quarterly revenue and lifted its outlook, yet its shares declined and failed to lift broader technology stocks. Investors remain concerned about valuations and the scale of spending required to sustain artificial-intelligence growth. Other AI-linked companies also weakened, while traders awaited Federal Reserve minutes and further signals on interest rates. Oil prices eased as higher US inventories offset some of the risk premium from renewed Gulf fighting. A single trading session does not establish a long-term reversal in the AI sector, but it shows how sensitive markets have become to expectations.

editorial.title: Political disputes must be settled by evidence and due process
editorial.imageAlt: Nigeria political and legal process context image
editorial.summary: The ADC appeal is now part of a legal process. INEC, political parties and the courts should act transparently while respecting due process.
editorial.content: The ADC's 17-ground appeal raises questions that must be resolved by the courts, not by political pressure or online speculation. The party's request to preserve its candidate records is an application, not an order already granted. INEC should comply with valid court directions, explain its actions clearly and avoid prejudging the appeal. All political actors deserve equal treatment under the law, and voters deserve certainty before the 2027 election timetable advances.

analysis.title: Why attacks around Hormuz can affect economies far from the Gulf
analysis.imageAlt: Gulf shipping and maritime security illustration
analysis.summary: Threats to vessels can raise insurance, freight and energy costs even without a formal closure of the Strait of Hormuz.
analysis.content: The latest incident involving an ADNOC-linked vessel demonstrates how insecurity can affect commercial shipping. Ship operators may reroute, delay voyages or face higher insurance premiums. Energy traders also price in the possibility of supply disruption. Import-dependent economies in Asia, Europe and Africa can feel the impact through fuel, transport and production costs. The scale of the effect depends on how long the risk persists, whether traffic is disrupted and whether diplomatic efforts reduce tensions.

analysis.title: Sudan's drone war shows why civilian protection must be central to diplomacy
analysis.summary: The UN's verified casualty figures underline the impact of drone attacks on markets, hospitals, fuel supplies and other civilian infrastructure.
analysis.content: The UN's latest figures are a minimum verified count, not the full human cost. Drone attacks have affected essential services and livelihoods far from front lines. Humanitarian access, protection of civilian infrastructure, independent investigations and accountability should be priorities in any diplomatic initiative. The parties to the conflict must comply with international humanitarian law regardless of their military objectives.

beyondStatement.title: An appeal is not the same as a court order
beyondStatement.imageAlt: Nigeria court and party leadership dispute context
beyondStatement.summary: The ADC has filed an appeal and asked for interim protection of candidate records. The request must not be reported as an order already granted.
beyondStatement.content: The distinction matters. A party can file grounds of appeal and ask the Court of Appeal for interim relief, but the court must decide whether to grant that relief. Until an order is made, the legal position should be described precisely. Readers should look for the court's actual ruling and any official INEC response.

beyondStatement.title: Verified minimums are not the full toll
beyondStatement.summary: The UN's verified civilian death toll in Sudan is a minimum count based on documented cases; the actual toll is likely higher.
beyondStatement.content: Conflict casualty figures often change as investigators gain access to affected areas. The UN's 2,230 figure is a verified minimum for January to October 2026. It should not be presented as a complete final total. Accurate reporting preserves the time period, verification method and warning about undercounting.

publicInterestFeature.title: Sudan's civilian toll: the human cost behind the numbers
publicInterestFeature.imageAlt: Sudan humanitarian crisis and civilian protection, contextual illustration
publicInterestFeature.summary: The UN's latest verified figures show the impact of drone attacks on hospitals, markets, fuel supplies and essential services.
publicInterestFeature.content: At least 2,230 civilians were verified killed in Sudan between January and October 2026, according to the UN Human Rights Office. More than 1,630 deaths were linked to drone strikes. The UN says the actual toll is likely higher. The report documents attacks affecting markets, hospitals, schools, fuel facilities, water sources and civilian vehicles. The figures are not just a measure of battlefield violence: they describe damage to the systems that keep families alive. Protection of civilians, safe humanitarian access and accountability must be central to any effort to end the conflict.
